sessionName: Week 7 - Marketing campaign and thought leadership
summary: George Berrington ran a marketing session with Joanna Pike and Oliver Grant to put the operating partner narrative into campaigns. We agreed a single annual research piece on people risk in buy-and-build deals and a Joanna-led LinkedIn presence. The logistics case study from Week 2 is now approved and will anchor the first campaign.

discussion.keyPoints: Joanna has spoken at two HR conferences but nothing aimed at PE audiences. Oliver suggested a survey of operating partners on post-deal people issues.
Joanna was reluctant to post regularly. George argued that operating partners buy from the person, and a modest cadence would be enough.
The logistics client has agreed to be named. Oliver wants a second case study from a software buy-and-build but sign-off is uncertain.

recommendations.recommendation: Publish an annual People Risk in Buy-and-Build report based on a survey of at least 50 operating partners, launched at the Q1 roundtable.
Joanna to post on LinkedIn twice a week, focused on post-deal people lessons.
Release the named logistics case study (94% key people retained) as the first campaign asset this month.
Measure each campaign by operating partner meetings booked, with a target of 4 meetings per campaign.
Produce a monthly newsletter for portfolio CHROs.

nextFocus: Build referral and partnership routes into PE houses.
nextPreparation: Joanna to list firms that regularly sit alongside Larkspur on deals, such as financial DD providers and executive search.

tests.question: What did we agree about the annual research report?
Is Joanna posting on LinkedIn twice a week agreed?
How are we measuring campaign success?
